newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistani newspapers - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistani newspapers - July 15.

text.p: (These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.)
TOP STORIES OF THE DAY
THE NATION
* Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan will visit Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan from Tuesday.
THE NEWS
* Pakistan is planning to introduce more stringent laws to curb sectarian violence in the country.
* Hameedullah Khan, brother of Aimal Kansi who is accused of killing CIA employees, and the family's lawyer Amjad Rashid will leave for the United States this week.
DAWN

* As many as 389 fishermen incarcerated in Pakistan and India since 1993 will be released on Tuesday. However, the fate of over 300 other civilian prisoners held by both the countries still hangs in balance.
* Pakistan and the IMF will undertake their first round of formal talks on Tuesday to discuss budget deficit as well as financial and banking reforms undertaken by Islamabad.
* The Mari Gas Co Ltd has announced the discovery of natural gas reserves in its Mari lease area located in the southern province of Sindh.
* Interior Minister Shujaat Hussain said the paramilitary Frontier Constabulary would be deployed for the security of embassies and foreign missions.
* Pakistan has formally requested the Saudi government on humanitarian grounds to release the Pakistani children recently arrested with alleged drug smugglers in the kingdom.
* The government will get back the management of the United Bank Ltd from the State (central) Bank of Pakistan on Tuesday.

* The PTA plant worth 16.8 billion rupees being constructed by ICI Pakistan at Port Qasim will go to DuPont as part of its global acquisition of ICI's white pigment business outside North America and worldwide polyester film, resin, intermediate business and all related technologies.
BUSINESS RECORDER
* Water and Power Minister Haleem Siddiqui who is also chairman of the task force for ports and shipping said the Karachi Port was incurring an annual loss of $780 million.
* The state-run Pakistan International Airlines announced a 10 percent increase in domestic fares effective from July 15.
* Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said Pakistan has agreed to allow Iran to transport natural gas to India through a pipeline passing through Pakistan.
* Orix Leasing Pakistan has formed the first leasing comapny in Egypt in partnership with leading Egyptian and international financial institutions.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
